edits.old: MongoDB driver tickets report that network and server latency variation can still make the client hit its socket timeout before reading the server's `MaxTimeMSExpired` response, causing connection churn. A Go Driver experiment reported that with CSOT budgets below one second, no derived `maxTimeMS` value allowed the server to respond before the client deadline. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-22)

edits.old: In the Java Sync driver's documented behavior, `timeoutMS` is unset by default, a positive value bounds operation completion, and `0` means operations do not time out; the CSOT specification likewise says an unset value leaves existing timeout behavior in place and `0` means infinite, though some specific client-side timeouts can still apply. (high confidence)
edits.new: The Java Sync driver documents that a positive timeoutMS value sets the timeout for operation completion, `0` means operations never time out, and `null` or unset defers to the legacy timeout settings. The CSOT specification says the default value is unset, which leaves existing timeout behavior unchanged, and that an explicit `0` means infinite, though some client-side timeouts like serverSelectionTimeoutMS still apply. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/java/sync/current/connection/specify-connection-options/csot/ ; https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/client-side-operations-timeout/client-side-operations-timeout.md
